title: DenseOpenVanishingComparison
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field and P=(X,A) a curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting] with constructible torsion abelian sheaf A [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion]. Let U be a dense open of X, j its inclusion, and B=j_!j^*A [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Use the coefficient equivalence E from abelian groups to modules over ULift Z, defined by the inverse of the forgetful equivalence from Z-modules followed by restriction of scalars along ULift Z ≃ Z. Put F=E(A) and G=E(B). Write T(F) for the alternative that F has invertible-order torsion or is p-primary for a prime p=char(k) [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion]. For every q>1 there exists an additive equivalence H^q(X,G) ≃ H^q(X,F). Moreover C3(G) implies C3(F), and under T(F), C3(F) implies C3(G), where C3 is primary vanishing [def-weil-pbc-C3].

proof.text: The coefficient functor E is a composite of equivalences. It preserves colimits and sheafification. Use Mathlib Functor.lanCompIsoOfPreserves and sheafComposeNatIso to commute E with the Kan-extension descriptions of upperStar and openImmersionLowerShriek. This gives an isomorphism from G to the module-valued extension by zero of F. Cohomology of a sheaf isomorphism is an additive equivalence, by Sheaf.H.map_comp_apply.

Apply dense_open_high_cohomology to F with coefficient ring ULift Z and curve map P.toSpec. Its first clause is a bijective additive counit map in every degree q>1. Convert it using AddEquiv.ofBijective and compose with the equivalence of step 1.

Apply shortExact_openClosedShortComplex to P.F and the complementary closed immersion U.closedComplement. Its first map is the abelian dense-open counit and is monic. The coefficient functor on sheaves preserves finite limits, since sheafToPresheaf creates limits and E preserves limits. Hence it gives a monomorphism G to F. Each geometric stalk functor preserves finite limits, so the map on stalk modules is injective. Pull back the witnesses p^n x=0, or n x=0 with n invertible on the base, along that injection. Thus primary torsion and invertible-order torsion pass from F to G.

Given C3(G), fix a characteristic prime p and assume F is p-primary. Step 3 makes G p-primary; apply C3(G) and transfer Subsingleton along the inverse of the additive equivalence of step 2. For the reverse implication when F is r-primary for a characteristic prime r, CharP.eq identifies r with p. Apply C3(F) and transfer Subsingleton along the equivalence of step 2.

For the remaining reverse case, assume F has invertible-order torsion and G is p-primary for a prime characteristic p. Step 3 gives invertible-order torsion of G. At each geometric stalk, choose p^a and an invertible integer n annihilating an element. Map the unit condition along Scheme.ΓSpecIso to k. Then p does not divide n, by CharP.cast_eq_zero; hence Nat.Prime.coprime_iff_not_dvd and Nat.Coprime.pow_left make p^a and n coprime. The Mathlib lemma nsmul_eq_zero_iff_of_coprime makes the element zero. Scheme.sheafHom_ext_of_sheafFiber_map_algClosurePoint makes the identity of G equal to zero; IsZero.iff_id_eq_zero gives IsZero G. Apply the additive forgetful functor and Sheaf.subsingleton_H_of_isZero. Pair the three conclusions.
